risk: Tenant requests below-market rent, concessions, or repairs; extension economics underperform current value.
mitigation: Get written term sheet early; inspect lease obligations and compare extension net present value to independent sale alternatives.
trigger: Extension offer below the after-tax hold-vs-sale hurdle.

risk: Tenant's restaurant performance or credit weakens; rent interruption or default occurs.
mitigation: Verify actual guarantor and credit; assess lease remedies, security, reletting downtime and alternative tenant demand.
trigger: Credit deterioration, missed rent, closure signals, or refusal to provide estoppel.

risk: Repairs, environmental issues, or landlord carve-outs cost more than expected under the NNN lease.
mitigation: Review actual lease allocation, inspections, maintenance records, environmental reports and reserves.
trigger: Unbudgeted capital needs or material landlord obligations found.

risk: Earthquake damages the structure, access, utilities or surrounding business demand; business interruption or retrofit costs follow.
mitigation: Parcel/building-specific engineering and insurance review, seismic retrofit evaluation, continuity plan, adequate limits and deductible reserve.
trigger: Engineer or insurer identifies unacceptable residual exposure.

risk: Wildfire/smoke, flood, extreme heat or another disaster causes physical damage, closure, insurance loss or broader regional disruption.
mitigation: Map verified parcel hazards; obtain written commercial coverage terms and exclusions; stress downtime, deductibles and uninsurable loss.
trigger: Coverage unavailable/uneconomic or residual loss exceeds tolerable reserve.

risk: Tenant bankruptcy or site closure coincides with poor leasing market; vacant land produces little/no rent and incurs carrying costs.
mitigation: Model vacancy duration and tenant-improvement/leasing costs; retain liquidity and test alternative use/rezoning constraints.
trigger: Verified competing use cannot support land value or likely downtime exceeds reserve.

risk: Sale occurs at a discount because remaining lease term, rent, tenant credit, or marketing window is unattractive.
mitigation: Get confidential broker opinions and appraisal under multiple lease-duration assumptions; time marketing using actual notice calendar.
trigger: Net bids fail owner's documented after-tax hurdle.

risk: Selling costs, taxes, debt payoff, or deferred maintenance reduce proceeds below headline price.
mitigation: CPA/attorney net-proceeds schedule and title/payoff review before accepting an offer.
trigger: Net-proceeds estimate materially below buyer price impression.

risk: Sale proceeds are reinvested at lower returns, higher fees, duration risk, or concentration risk than assumed.
mitigation: Compare credible replacement opportunities net of fees/taxes, liquidity and downside; use conservative ranges and reserve cash.
trigger: No implementable replacement plan meets required risk-adjusted net hurdle.

risk: Disaster or market shock during marketing causes damage, tenant disruption, unavailable insurance, financing repricing, or buyer withdrawal.
mitigation: Confirm coverage and sale contract risk allocation; update disclosure and pricing; do not represent hazard as absent based on regional averages.
trigger: Material incident or insurance/financing term change before close.

risk: Large regional earthquake, wildfire or infrastructure failure degrades local liquidity and sale comps; buyer financing and insurance become constrained.
mitigation: Do not anchor price on historic cap rates alone; use marketability stress, insurance quotes, downtime, and a hold fallback.
trigger: Material deterioration in bid depth, insurer appetite, or access/utilities.

risk: Delay misses lease notice/option dates, reduces saleability as expiry approaches, or concentrates wealth in one tenant and site.
mitigation: Maintain counsel-verified milestone calendar and quarterly decision review; preserve sale and extension alternatives.
trigger: First contractual notice deadline or market/credit deterioration.

risk: Black-swan event causes permanent impairment while owner remains exposed to tenant, structure, geography and local market.
mitigation: Estimate tail loss with parcel/engineering evidence; maintain insurance and liquidity; diversify outside the property where consistent with goals.
trigger: Uninsured tail loss exceeds a privately set tolerance or diversification threshold.

risk: Regional economic contraction, consumer spending weakness, employment softness, higher financing costs or lower transaction liquidity reduces tenant resilience, sale pricing, or replacement returns.
mitigation: Stress lower rent/tenant performance, longer marketing and vacancy periods, wider exit-yield range, financing changes and lower reinvestment returns; refresh official labor and macro data before decision dates.
trigger: Material deterioration in tenant disclosures, BLS trends, buyer depth, lender terms or replacement yield.
